subject: Sunrise Health — observability & PII handling: post-call summary & actions
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sen <priya@sunrisehealth.io>, security@sunrisehealth.io
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sunrise Health — observability & PII handling: post-call summary & actions

Hi Priya (and team),

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick write-up of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone has the same view.

Summary of pain points (as discussed)
- Production prompts and user messages currently surface protected health information that cannot be stored in plain text logs.
- Existing logging pipeline (S3 + Datadog) is used for monitoring; engineering can’t send PII to third-party SaaS without redaction.
- Need per-tenant audit logs and an auditable retention policy (security wants 30-day max by default).
- Encryption at-rest with customer-managed keys is required for any persisted artifacts.

Current stack you described
- In-house frontend + microservices on AWS (EKS)
- Logs → S3 (lifecycle rules) → Datadog for alerts
- Prototype LLM service (internal) used for triage; no stable rollout yet

Success criteria you gave
- No PII persisted in cleartext in logs or long-term storage (redaction or token-level hashing).
- Ability to produce tenant-scoped audit trail for every inference request (who/when/model variant).
- Demonstrable retention enforcement and proof for audits.

What Redwood can offer (high level)
- Prefix/KV caching and optional in-flight redaction (remove or token-replace PII before logs are emitted).
- Configurable retention rules and per-tenant audit log export; can integrate with customer KMS for key management.
- Fallback model variants for degraded capacity to preserve SLAs while respecting privacy constraints.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) I’m attaching a small PII Mapping template — please fill the top examples and return (Priya) by EOD Wed so we can confirm redaction surface (owner: Priya).
2) Engineering + security deep-dive with our infra/security engineer (Rishi) — propose Thu 04/17 10:00–11:00 PT (owner: Jasmine / Rishi).
3) Demo window (non-prod) showing redaction + retention enforcement — tentatively week of 4/24 (owner: Jasmine).
4) We’ll send a short note of compliance artifacts (SOC2, logs sample) after the security call (owner: Marcus).

Attachments included: PII_Mapping_Template.xlsx, redwood-poc-overview.pdf

If I missed anything critical, flag it here — otherwise, Priya, can you confirm the suggested times and whether VPC/on-prem connectors are required for the POC?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
(415) 555-0134

From: Priya Sen <priya@sunrisehealth.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sunrise Security <security@sunrisehealth.io>
Date: 2027-04-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sunrise Health — observability & PII handling: post-call summary & actions

Jasmine — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications and additions from our side: 

- Confirmed: we cannot have PII in Datadog or any external logging SaaS. Logs that contain PHI must be redacted before export.
- We do need per-tenant redaction (different customers have variable consent rules).
- KMS requirement: all keys must be customer-managed (Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS BYOK). We’re primarily on AWS today but we have an on-prem HSM for high-sensitivity tenants.
- For the POC, we prefer a VPC connector (no public egress) — we will provide a jump host and temporary firewall rule for the demo if needed.

We’ll start filling out the PII_Mapping_Template and return a first pass by EOD Wednesday. For the deep-dive, Thu 04/17 10:00 PT works for engineering + security.

Also: can you attach a brief note describing audit-log retention choices (30/90/365 days) and the default Redwood recommendation for regulated customers? Security would like to see the options before the call.

Priya Sen
Head of Product Security | Sunrise Health
priya@sunrisehealth.io

---
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sen <priya@sunrisehealth.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sunrise Security <security@sunrisehealth.io>
Date: 2027-04-15T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sunrise Health — observability & PII handling: post-call summary & actions

Thanks Priya — great, appreciate the quick turnaround.

A few confirmations and prep items before Thu: 
- I’m attaching a short note that outlines our retention profiles (redwood-privacy-options.md) — TL;DR: default is 30 days for full logs, 90 days for metadata-only; we can support shorter windows and automatic redaction at ingest.
- For KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS BYOK) and can work with your on-prem HSM via our private connector. We’ll have Rishi bring a short diagram to the call to show network/configuration requirements.
- VPC connector: noted — we’ll provide an architecture sketch for the POC that keeps egress within your VPC and uses a temporary peering/jump host.

Proposed agenda for Thu 04/17 10:00–11:00 PT
1) Security goals & constraints (Sunrise) — 10m
2) Network/KMS/keys (Redwood infra) — 15m
3) Demo: redaction + retention enforcement in a sandbox (Redwood) — 20m
4) POC scoping & timeline (mutual) — 10m
5) Next steps & owners — 5m

I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu and include a link to the PII template in Drive. Marcus will drop the SOC2 artifacts into the Drive folder prior to the call.

Best,
Jasmine

Attachment: redwood-privacy-options.md
